title: Priyadarshan Lost Hera Pheri 3. So He Called Akshay Kumar Instead.
excerpt: The director-actor duo who gave us Bhagam Bhag, Garam Masala, and De Dana Dan are reuniting for a comedy thriller that Priyadarshan says he's never attempted before
body:
There's a version of this story where Priyadarshan spends the second half of 2026 directing *Hera Pheri 3*, bringing back the chaos of Raju, Shyam, and Baburao one more time. That version doesn't exist anymore.

Producer Firoz Nadiadwala confirmed earlier this year that Priyadarshan would not be directing the long-awaited sequel. Priyadarshan himself verified it, putting to rest years of speculation. The *Hera Pheri* trilogy — arguably the most quoted comedy franchise in Indian cinema history — will continue, but without the man who started it.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Zadw9-bDXGo

Here's what happened next: Priyadarshan picked up the phone and called Akshay Kumar.

Film Number Nine

According to a report by *Mid-Day*, Priyadarshan's next directorial will be a comedy thriller starring Akshay in the lead. The film is being produced by Tips and is expected to go on floors by December 2026.

Priyadarshan has written the story himself. Rohan Shankar, who co-wrote the screenplay for their recent reunion film *Bhooth Bangla*, will develop the screenplay alongside him.

> **"## What "Never Attempted Before" Actually Means

Priyadarshan has done slapstick."**

> "Priyadarshan has written the story, which is a combination of fun and thrills. He feels this belongs to a genre that he hasn't attempted before." — Source to Mid-Day

When contacted, Priyadarshan kept it simple: *"My next film is with Akshay Kumar and Tips."*

That's nine films together. Nine. A partnership that began with *Hera Pheri* in 2000 and has since produced *Bhagam Bhag* (2006), *Garam Masala* (2005), *De Dana Dan* (2009), *Khatta Meetha* (2010), *Tees Maar Khan* (2010), *Bhool Bhulaiyaa* (2007), and most recently *Bhooth Bangla* — the horror comedy that marked their reunion after a lengthy gap.

What "Never Attempted Before" Actually Means

Priyadarshan has done slapstick. He's done horror comedy. He's done social satire. He's done everything involving Paresh Rawal looking exasperated while someone runs into a glass door. What he hasn't done — at least not in Hindi cinema — is a *proper* thriller with comedic DNA. Not a comedy with thriller elements, but a thriller that happens to be funny. The distinction matters.

Akshay, meanwhile, has been on a tear. *Welcome to the Jungle* just crossed ₹100 crore with no upfront fee — he bet on profit-sharing and won. *Bhooth Bangla* performed respectably.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaPRm2ZtPNE/

He's also attached to *Haiwaan* with Priyadarshan and Saif Ali Khan, which means the director-actor pair currently have *two* films in various stages of development.

The timing is interesting. Priyadarshan had reportedly been developing a dramedy with Pankaj Tripathi and a film with Mohanlal, but both have been postponed. The Akshay project has jumped the queue, which suggests either the script demanded immediacy or the commercial logic was too compelling to ignore.

For the Diaspora: Why This Matters More Than You Think

If you grew up in an Indian household anywhere in the US, UK, or Canada, there's a better-than-even chance that *Hera Pheri* and *Bhagam Bhag* were in heavy rotation. These aren't just films — they're family vocabulary. "Ye Baburao ka style hai" is a language unto itself. The Priyadarshan-Akshay comedies defined a particular era of Bollywood comfort viewing that diaspora families still return to on lazy weekends.

A new entry in that lineage — even without the Hera Pheri brand — carries enormous nostalgic weight. And the "comedy thriller" description suggests something with more edge than their 2000s output. Priyadarshan at his best has always been a technically precise filmmaker who happens to make people laugh; a thriller framework gives him structural discipline that pure comedies sometimes lack.

The film is expected to shoot through early 2027. No title yet. No co-stars announced beyond Akshay. Just a director who lost one project and immediately found something that excited him more — and an actor who's learned that betting on the right collaborator pays better than betting on a franchise.

Sometimes the sequel you don't get leads to the film you actually needed.
